To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a new approach, score embedding, for learning interpretable vector representations and apply this method on the Twitter sentiment analysis of Affordable Care Act.
we introduce score embedding which is a supervised method to learn interpretable word representations for sentiment analysis.
we have developed a novel method to learn vector representations for words that are interpretable and can capture the sentiment of words.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: 1) Can score embedding effectively incorporate sentiment information? 2) Is the sentiment information learned by score embedding consistent with human intuition? 3) Can the sentiment information learned using score embedding help us understand the public opinion on health care?

the following: 1) How does one learn interpretable vector representation for words? 2) How can we effectively use these representations to identify the public sentiment towards a particular issue? 3) Can we use these representations to compare the public sentiments towards different issues?
the analysis of public opinion on health care using the proposed score embeddings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our model can effectively learn the sentiment information from the training data and can be used for the sentiment analysis of the health care related discussions on Twitter.

our proposed score embedding method can be used to effectively analyze the public sentiment towards different health care plans and the results indicate that the public opinion towards the affordable care act has been positive.
our proposed method is effective and interpretable in capturing the sentiment and opinions about health care issues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the score embedding approach provides a novel and effective way for learning interpretable representations from labeled training data and our approach outperforms or at least comparable to state-of-the-art approaches for the sentiment classification task.
we have shown the effectiveness of score embedding for sentiment analysis and have used the proposed approach for identifying the public opinion regarding the health care issues.

we have shown the effectiveness of the score embedding model for learning interpretable vector representations of words and we have also shown the effectiveness of score embedding in capturing the sentiment information in the text.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can learn a model that can effectively incorporate sentiment and topic information and the model can be trained on a smaller corpus.
score embedding can be used to identify public opinion on a particular issue by analyzing the tweets on that issue.
score embedding can be used for sentiment analysis of health care issues and can be used as an alternative to other supervised and unsupervised learning approaches.
